pairs.question: Num maiore?
pairs.derivation: Authorial self-question and self-answer about Antonius's nobility relative to Catiline. The preceding 'Primum nobilitate eadem qua Catilina.' answers a separate question (quo splendore est?); here 'Num maiore?' ('Is it by greater nobility?') is answered curtly 'Non.' The window stops at the full stop; what follows ('Sed virtute. Quam ob rem?...') is a new exchange. Crux marks (+ +) around Catilina in the preceding sentence are kept out of this pair.

pairs.question: Quam ob rem?
pairs.answer: Quod Antonius umbram suam metuit, hic ne leges quidem.
pairs.derivation: Following 'Sed virtute' (he excels by virtue), the author asks 'Quam ob rem?' ('For what reason?') and answers it himself with a Quod-clause. End of the answer window placed at 'ne leges quidem' (the first full stop / clean contrast: Antonius fears his own shadow, this one not even the laws); what follows ('natus in patris egestate, educatus in sororiis stupris...') is elaboration/digression, so it is cut.
